REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 12, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021), this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
AUGUST 12, 2021, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were made by the City Council as follows:

  CDG Community Service (Cerritos Residents Against Asian Hate Crimes Rally).

  Bradley Nishida (Rank of Eagle Scout).

5B.  Informational update on the City's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational report was given by Laurie Kajiwara, Public Information Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  M. Villa expressed concerns regarding an Amazon Fresh store and Amazon’s business
  practices. She also supported the City Council’s resolution expressing a Vote of No
  Confidence in Los Angeles County District Attorney George Gascón.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7D.  Award of contract for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts lettershop and mailing
  services, Bid No. 1428-21 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Award a contract for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts lettershop and
  mailing services, Bid No. 1428-21, to Orange County Direct Mail in the amount of
  $14,218.00 with the following provisions:

  a. The term of the contract shall begin upon the City Council's award of bid and
  extends for 18 months; and

  b. The term of the agreement may be extended by mutual agreement of both
  parties for up to three additional 12-month terms. Upon the completion of the
  18-month period of the agreement, the lettershop and mailing services firm may
  request that the City approve an increase in the project fees for work to be
  completed for the additional period. Such requests for increase shall be based on
  the Consumer Price Index of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, U.S. Department of
  Labor, Los Angeles - Long Beach metropolitan area for the period of July 1
  through June 30 of the calendar year immediately preceding the date of such
  adjustment. The maximum increase for any period shall be 3 percent (COUNCIL).

  1. Award a contract for the printing of the 2022 Cerritos Community Calendar to

  2. In the event issues of non-performance arise, the project would be removed from
  Advantage Mailing, Inc. and taken to the next lowest bidder to ensure the City's
  printing deadline, quality standards and specifications are met. This process would
  be repeated as necessary in order of the lowest bid to the highest (COUNCIL).

  Fountain at the Cerritos Civic Center (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to;

  1. Find that staff has satisfied the purpose of the bidding statute of the Cerritos
  Municipal Code, and that it is reasonable and necessary to single source purchase
  the components required to restore the Dolphin Fountain water feature operation;
  and

  2. Approve the appropriation and expenditure of funds in the amount of $41,766.29
  from the Art in Public Places Trust Fund to restore the Dolphin Fountain; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to purchase the components required to complete water
  feature repairs, from Crystal Fountains, Inc., at a cost of $33,478.29; and

  4. Authorize the City Manager to approve the labor costs for Service First, Inc. to
  perform the installation of controller parts for the Dolphin Fountain at the Civic
  Center in the amount of $8,288; and

  5. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to approve any change orders that may
  become necessary to complete the scope of work discussed in this report (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of City of Cerritos participation in Cerritos Auto Square
  documentary video (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Laurie Kajiwara, Public Information Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Dave Conant, representing the Cerritos Auto Square Dealers Association, spoke in
  support of the subject project.

  Todd Huffman, representing Pipeline Digital Media, spoke in support of the subject
  project.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to:

  1. Participate in and support the production of a documentary video about the Cerritos
  Auto square; and

  2. Prepare a budget amendment in the amount of $25,000.00 as a maximum amount
  for the City to contribute towards the cost of the production; and

  3. Authorize payments to Pipeline Digital Media as outlined in the Terms described in
  the company’s proposal; and

  4. To include the appropriate language in the final contract to allow the City Council
  members and designated City of Cerritos staff to review the video prior to general
  release to the public (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
